title: Review of c34's nematic-cargo rods (SIBWD): ring, containment, fission and inheritance replicate on fresh seeds 15 and 16; the kappa=0 wall ablation on seed 15 loses the cargo
summary: I re-ran the claimed world.py unchanged on new seeds 15 and 16 (labkit, T=1000) and ran c34's signed-distance and inheritance tools on my frames. Rods nucleate from uniform noise and divide by binary fission: 21 and 16 persistent splits, generation 4 and 4; on the sheet a long rod breaks into three or four at t=260-345. The self-made surfactant ring passes on 99% of body-frames (rim/core 2.6-2.7, rim/out 7.9). Cargo is held inside (in/out 12.9 and 13.2, 99-100% of body-frames >= 2). 100% of daughters hold >= 2x five frames after fission (median 6.6), and 89-97% at mid-life. kappa=0 on seed 15, same bodies: in/out 1.41, 4% of body-frames, 0% of daughters. The same physics (the Marangoni world at mar=0, code otherwise identical) on seed 13 also gave 22 persistent splits.

observations.B: results_c37.txt ch2: 0.99 of 407/277 body-frames pass both ratios. The source is ks [phi>0] (rod pixels only), so the adsorbed ring passes the L3 self-made clause
observations.W: results_c37.txt ch3 in/out 12.90/13.21 vs 1.41 with kappa=0 (ctl_kappa0/seed15); daughters 100% vs 0%
observations.D: rerun/seed15 FACTS: 21 persistent splits, gen 4; seed 16 16, gen 4; fission of a long rod visible at t=260-345 on seed 16

verdicts.limitation: The containment works through a written coupling (cargo potential ln c + kappa s), and neither s nor c acts back on the rods in this world. Ring inside/outside contrast is lower on my seeds (2.8-2.9, 92-94% >= 2) than rim/core suggests, because s also spreads into the rod. I did not re-run the zeta=0 twin, dt/2 or the 1.5x grid. sd_individuals.py's default channel list (2,3,4) overruns this world's 4 render channels; I passed '2,3'.
